note: India: citizens of Nepal and Bhutan enter without a visa, and Maldivians for tourism, medical treatment or business stay under 90 days in six months without one (the Minister of State for External Affairs, Rajya Sabha, 19 December 2024). Japanese and South Korean nationals may take a visa on arrival (the UAE's only if they held an Indian visa before, so they are taken as e-Visa). Passport holders of the 174 countries and regions on the e-Visa list apply online and receive an electronic travel authorisation before flying, the e-Visa stamped on arrival (its stay is the e-Visa's: one month, one year or five years for tourism, at most 180 days a year). Everyone else, Pakistan's and China's nationals among them, applies for a regular visa.

sources.title: Government of India, Indian Visa Online: e-Visa (eligibility, FAQ)
sources.said: If you hold valid passports from any of the following countries/regions, you are eligible for eVisa. 1. Albania 2. Andorra ... 114. Netherlands 115. New Zealand ... 175. Zimbabwe ... The Visa on Arrival facility is only for the nationals of Japan, South Korea and UAE (only for such UAE nationals who had earlier obtained e-Visa or regular/paper visa for India). For the nationals of all other countries eligible for e-Visa, the e-visa application have to be filled online and the applicant must wait till the confirmation/Grant of ETA for travelling to India.

sources.title: All India Radio News (Prasar Bharati), written reply in the Rajya Sabha (19 December 2024)
sources.said: In a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha, Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh informed that India provides visa-free entry to citizens of Nepal, Bhutan and Maldives. He added that in the case of Maldives, their citizens intending to visit India for tourism, medical and business purposes are exempted from the requirement of a prior visa if their period of stay in India is less than 90 days in the preceding six months.
